# Research findings (REQUIREMENTS.md §14)

Source reviewed 2026-11-12: *Feasibility Study: Fully Automatic AC Discovery & Control App (Pakistan)*,
12 pages, supplied as `Feasibility Study_ Fully Automatic AC Discovery & Control App (Pakistan) (1).pdf`
(an earlier copy without "(1)" differs only slightly). This is taken to be the "Deep Research PDF" the
requirements refer to.

**How to read this document.** The study was generated by ChatGPT. Its citations (e.g. `【44†L27-L34】`)
refer to web pages that are not included, so none of its claims can be traced to a source from the
PDF alone. Every claim below is therefore a **lead**, not an established fact, unless the "Our
evidence" column says otherwise. Where the study conflicts with something this project has verified
or implemented, both are recorded and the conflict is listed in §4.

## 1. Overall conclusions of the study

| Study conclusion | Our position |
|---|---|
| A truly universal app is not possible; IR-only ACs and cloud-only Wi-Fi modules cannot be found or controlled over the LAN. | Agreed. Help screen now says so in plain words (§5). |
| Broad coverage of the main Pakistani smart-AC brands is feasible with a plug-in adapter per protocol. | Matches the architecture already built (ARCHITECTURE.md). |
| Each ecosystem needs a one-time, authorised account login to obtain device keys. | True for Haier and (reportedly) Midea v3; **not** needed for Gree, which pairs over the LAN (§4, conflict 2). Haier login conflicts with "do not hardcode secrets" (§4, conflict 1). |
| Control must stay local after setup and work with the internet off. | Implemented: no cloud traffic in any implemented path. Not yet tested on a phone (TEST_REPORT.md §4). |
| Keys stored with Android Keystore; never hardcoded or exposed. | Implemented (SECURITY.md). |
| Warn about routers with AP/guest isolation when ACs cannot be reached. | Already shown on the pairing screen when nothing is found. |
| Mark detected but unsupported devices as "unsupported – cloud-only" and advise the user. | Partly: only devices that answer a supported protocol can be detected at all. Help text added (§5). |
| Elderly users: scan automatically, log in once, one card per AC, no technical detail. | Matches the current UI (auto scan on the pairing screen, brand-neutral rows). |
| Suggested order: Haier → Gree → Midea/AUX/TCL → Dawlance (Arçelik) → Daikin → others. | Same as the requirements' integration order, except the requirements put Dawlance after TCL and Orient/PEL after Daikin, which the study also does. No change. |

## 2. Market share claims

The study gives Haier ~45 % (H1 2026), and from a 2022 blog Haier ~32 %, Gree ~22 %, Orient ~16 %,
PEL ~6 %, Dawlance ~4 %. Its own brand table later gives Orient "6 % share", contradicting the 16 %
above. None of these figures can be checked from the PDF. **The brand priorities in REQUIREMENTS.md
remain the ones used**; the study's ranking is broadly consistent with them.

## 3. Per-brand findings

| Brand | Study's claim (lead) | Our evidence / status | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Haier** | HaiSmart: TCP 56800, per-device key from Haier cloud via account login; `haismart-local` (MIT) does discovery, key retrieval and control; discovery described as "DHCP/MAC broadcast"; protocol called "Haier XML". | TCP 56800 and per-device cloud key: **consistent** with our implementation. Discovery: **verified on the owner's unit (2026-11-11)** to be UDISCOVERY on UDP 7083, not DHCP; device ID is the module MAC (540853BD1D41, matching the study's example). Frames are binary uSS, not XML. haismart-local MIT licence: checked when the driver was ported (THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). | Status/control test needs the local key. In-app login: see conflict 1. |
| **Gree** (and OEMs: Tosot, Toyotomi, Cooper & Hunter, Tadiran, Heiwa, Ekokai, Wilfa…) | UDP 7000; per-device key "extracted from the Gree app's data or cloud"; some newer modules are **cloud-only** (nothing listens on UDP 7000). | UDP 7000: **consistent**. Key: our adapter obtains it automatically with the LAN bind exchange (PROTOCOL_GREE.md), so no extraction or account is needed — **not yet tested on hardware**. Cloud-only modules: plausible; such units will simply not be found. | Test on a real unit. If a unit is found by the Gree app but not by ours, record it as "Issue identified – cloud-only module". |
| **Midea / AUX / TCL** | Many units use Midea's IoT module; local control after obtaining a **token + key from the Midea cloud** (protocol v1/v2/v3, AES); discovery "port 6666 or mDNS"; control "TCP 6666 (or HTTP?)"; libraries `midea_ac_lan`, `midea-ac-py`, claimed MIT. | Not implemented. Ports given by the study are hedged by the study itself. Community implementations we know of use UDP 6445 for discovery and TCP 6444 for control — **unverified by us**; must be confirmed with a capture. Whether AUX and TCL units in Pakistan actually carry Midea modules is unknown (study says "likely"). Licences not checked. | Capture a discovery reply from a real Midea, AUX and TCL unit. Then decide on v3 token provisioning (same issue as conflict 1). |
| **Dawlance** | Arçelik ecosystem (hOn / HomeWhiz); Home Assistant HomeWhiz integration works over local Bluetooth or the cloud depending on model; credential probably needs an account. | Nothing verified. Note the study's own quote says control is via **Bluetooth or the cloud**, so a local Wi-Fi path is not established. Bluetooth would add a permission the app does not have today. | Capture from a real unit; confirm which app the Pakistani Dawlance Wi-Fi models use. |
| **Daikin** | Wi-Fi controllers (BRP069/BRP072); auto-discovery; "UDP 30050, no key unless a password was set". | Not implemented. Our understanding from community code (pydaikin) is that UDP 30050 is used for **discovery** and control is over HTTP (and HTTPS with a key on some adapters) — **unverified by us**. | Capture from a real adapter before implementing. |
| **Orient** | Smart lineup unclear; possibly no Wi-Fi models or a Midea-derived module. | Unknown. | Confirm a Wi-Fi model exists, then capture. |
| **PEL** | Possibly rebadged Fujitsu/Carrier tech; "likely not Wi-Fi by default". | Unknown. | As Orient. |
| **Panasonic** | Comfort Cloud; "local control on some units via port 443 with a token"; not researched in depth. | Unknown; the study marks it as not examined. | Low priority (requirements order 10). |
| **LG / Samsung** | ThinQ / SmartThings, cloud-only; no known LAN API; treat as unsupported. | Unknown. | Keep "Not started"; confirm before ruling out. |
| **Kenwood** | Only mentioned as appearing in price lists. | Unknown. | Capture first. |
| **Matter** | Few ACs certified (e.g. some Hisense portables); none of the major split brands. | — | Future work. |

## 4. Conflicts between the study and this project

1. **Haier key by in-app account login.** The study recommends logging in to the HaiSmart cloud
   inside the app to fetch keys automatically. Doing that requires the HaiSmart app's own client
   credentials to be built into this app. The requirements say "do not hardcode secrets" and "use
   authorized authentication", so the app still asks for the key once (DISCOVERY_AND_AUTH.md).
   **Update 2026-11-13:** the new specification (§4.2) requires in-app retrieval through the HaiSmart
   account, so it is implemented (DISCOVERY_AND_AUTH.md). The app identity is kept out of Git. The
   remaining owner decision is whether to distribute publicly on that basis. Original note: either accept the requirement as it stands, or
   obtain an authorised API from Haier, or explicitly accept the trade-off. The same question will
   arise for Midea v3 tokens.
2. **Gree key.** The study says the Gree key must be extracted from the app or cloud. The Gree
   module's own LAN bind exchange returns it, and that is what our adapter uses. Hardware will settle
   it; if a module refuses to bind, that unit is recorded as an issue.
3. **Location permission.** The study says `ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION` is needed for discovery. Android
   only requires it for Wi-Fi scan results and the network name; plain UDP/TCP to local addresses
   does not need it (the study itself says so a few lines later). The app, which has no location
   permission, identified and reached the real Haier unit from an emulator (TEST_REPORT.md); a
   broadcast scan from a real phone is still untested.
   The app keeps **no location permission**, per "request only required permissions".
4. **Haier discovery method.** Study: DHCP/MAC broadcast. Verified on hardware: UDISCOVERY on UDP 7083.
5. **Licences.** The study states gree-remote, the Midea repositories and HomeWhiz are MIT. We
   verified that **greeclimate, the Gree reference actually used, is GPL-3.0** (facts only were
   used; THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). The other licence claims are unchecked and must be checked before
   any code from those projects is used.
6. **Gree app name.** The study names "M-Smart" as a Gree app; M-Smart is Midea's app. Treated as
   an error in the study, with no effect on the code.
7. **Manual IP entry fallback.** Suggested by the study for networks that block broadcast. The app
   already sweeps the subnet by unicast, which works without broadcast, and the requirements keep
   addresses out of the normal UI. Not added.

## 5. Changes made from this review

- `docs/COMPATIBILITY_MATRIX.md`: brand roadmap "Research leads" filled from §3, labelled as unverified.
- Help screen: explains that ACs controlled only by a hand remote (no Wi-Fi) and Wi-Fi models that only work through the manufacturer's online service cannot be found by the app.
- `docs/PROGRESS.md`: "PDF not supplied" removed; conflict 1 listed as an open decision.
